text:
Predicates:
TwinOrTriplet(x) ::: x is a twin or triplet.
SpendTimeWithSiblings(x) ::: x spends a lot of time hanging out with and playing with siblings.
HaveSiblingsSameAge(x, y) ::: x has siblings y who are the same age.
ComplainsOften(x) ::: x complains often about annoying siblings.
LiveAtHomeRegularly(x) ::: x lives at home regularly.
DevelopsStrongBonds(x) ::: x develops strong bonds with family members.
Sibling(x, y) ::: x is a sibling of y.
Age(x, y) ::: x and y are the same age.

Premises:
∀x (TwinOrTriplet(x) → SpendTimeWithSiblings(x)) ::: If people are twins or triplets, then they spend a lot of time with siblings.
∀x ∀y (HaveSiblingsSameAge(x, y) → TwinOrTriplet(x)) ::: If people have siblings who are same age, then they are twins or triplets.
∀x (ComplainsOften(x) → ∃y (Sibling(x, y) ∧ Age(x, y))) ::: If people complain often about siblings, then they have siblings who are the same age.
∀x (¬LiveAtHomeRegularly(x) → ¬DevelopsStrongBonds(x)) ::: If people do not live at home regularly, then they do not develop strong bonds.
∀x (SpendTimeWithSiblings(x) → ¬LiveAtHomeRegularly(x)) ::: If people spend a lot of time with siblings, then they do not live at home regularly.
∀x ( (TwinOrTriplet(x) ∧ DevelopsStrongBonds(x)) ∨ (¬TwinOrTriplet(x) ∧ ¬DevelopsStrongBonds(x)) ) ::: Luke is either both a twin or triplet and develops strong bonds, or neither.
